name: Challenge #08: Turtle - Triangle
description:
🖌️ How to Fill a Shape in Turtle

To fill shapes in Turtle, we use two functions:

Function
Purpose

begin_fill()
Tells Turtle to start recording the shape outline

end_fill()
Fills the shape drawn between begin_fill() and end_fill()

⚠️ Important:
Everything drawn between begin_fill() and end_fill() will be filled with the active fill color.

Example:

import turtle

screen = turtle.Screen()
pen = turtle.Turtle()

pen.fillcolor("yellow")   # Set fill color
pen.begin_fill()          # Start filling
pen.circle(80)            # Draw a circle
pen.end_fill()            # End filling

pen.hideturtle()
screen.exitonclick()

Challenge :

A triangle where all the sides are of the same length is called an equilateral triangle. For this challenge, draw an equilateral triangle and fill it with a color. Save the code in a file called Challenge8.py.

• It ends with "THE END" (ignore the case).

The program should:

• Take input from the user (the story).

• Check all three conditions in a case-insensitive way.

• Print True if all conditions are met, otherwise print False.

• Print which condition(s) failed if the story is not magical.

Example:

Output: True

Take one down and pass it along, 1 bottle of milk on the wall.

name: Challenge #46: Functions - Driver Speed Evaluation Simulation
description:
In this challenge, you will build a program that simulates multiple driving events and calculates demerit points based on how fast a driver travels compared to a randomly selected speed limit.

Your solution will include two functions:

Function 1 (helper function): evaluate_drive(avg_speed, speed_limit)

Purpose

Evaluates a driver’s average speed against a given speed limit, and returns the number of demerit points earned.

Rules

• If the driver’s speed is within or below the speed limit, return 0 points.

• If the driver exceeds the speed limit:

• Award 1 demerit point for every 10 km/h over the speed limit
(e.g., 15 km/h over → 1 point; 25 km/h over → 2 points)

Return Value

•
An integer representing the number of demerit points.

Function 2 (primary function): run_driver_simluation()

Purpose

Runs a full simulation of multiple driving events, using evaluate_drive() to determine the demerit points for each drive.

Steps

• Display a simulation header.

• Create a list of possible speed limits:[50, 60, 70, 80]

• Ask the user how many drives they want to evaluate.

• For each simulated drive:

•

• Randomly choose a speed limit from the list using random.choice().

• Randomly generate the driver’s speed (within ±40 km/h of the speed limit).

• Pass both values to evaluate_drive() and get the demerit points.

• Add the returned demerit points to a running total.

• Print:

• Speed limit

• Driver speed

• Demerit points from the drive

• Total accumulated demerit points

• If total demerit points reach 12 or more, stop the simulation immediately and print:

•

• "Immediate suspension triggered!"

• "License suspended. You cannot continue driving."

• After all drives finish (or an early stop), print the final result.

Program Execution

At the end of the file, call:

run_driver_simluation()

to start the simulation.

Hints

random.choice()

random.choice(sequence) selects one random element from a list (or any sequence).

Example:

speed_limits = [50, 60, 70, 80]
speed_limit = random.choice(speed_limits)

This will randomly assign one of the values (50, 60, 70, or 80) to speed_limit each time it is called.

This allows every simulated drive to have a different speed limit.

🐢 Project Introduction — “The Great Turtle Grand Prix”

Welcome to the Great Turtle Grand Prix, where six fearless, color-splashed champions line up on a dazzling track for the race of a lifetime!
Each turtle is unique, each lane is vibrant, and only one will claim the glory.
In this whimsical and colorful showdown, chance determines victory—every step forward is a surprise!
So sit back and cheer on your favorite racer as they sprint (well… turtle-sprint) toward the checkered finish line!

📘 Project Synopsis

This project uses Python’s turtle graphics module to create a playful race between multiple turtles.
Along a decorated racetrack, turtles move forward by random distances, simulating an unpredictable race.
The first turtle to cross the finish line is crowned the winner, followed by a celebratory announcement and fireworks.
The project emphasizes simple animation, randomness, and interactivity—making it a fun beginner-friendly way to explore Python graphics.

Create the Game

Prepare the Racers

• Create multiple turtle racers in different colors.

• Position them at the starting line.

•
Run the Race

• Use a loop to move each turtle forward randomly.

• Continue until one crosses the finish line.

Declare the Winner

• Identify the turtle that finishes first.

 Keep the Window Open
